messages:
Alex G: noticing a weird pattern in us-west2 today — small gpu jobs get scheduled then immediately restart a few minutes later. logs show a flurry of network errors on a handful of nodes.
Priya N: saw that too, spikes of `rx_dropped` on nic counters, plus kernel oops on node-az2-11 around the same window.
Jin H: is it the usual nvlink/driver mismatch or something else? those cause packing to fail for gang jobs.
Alex G: not driver mismatch — nodes passed preflight last week. packet traces show retransmits between rack switch and host on az2-11..az2-13.
infra-bot: [alert] node-az2-11: 15% packet_loss over 5m, pod churn +120%
Ops Sam: can we cordon az2-11 and let scheduler rebalance?
Priya N: if we cordon one node, packing will scatter across azs and increase cross-az NVLink requirements; that will break gang scheduling for large jobs.
Maria C: consequences: higher latency and 2x reserved GPU hours while jobs wait for compatible placement. cost spike observable in the last 2 hours.
Jin H: suggestion: temporarily reduce strict inter-gpu affinity for batch jobs and let small ones backfill on remaining healthy nodes. then we can isolate the bad rack without killing throughput.
Alex G: config change would be `scheduler.alpha/allow-relaxed-gang=true` for the rollout canary. want to try on us-west2 only.
Priya N: +1 for canary but add a label so we don't accidentally relax prod criticals. `node.k8s.redwood/gpu-critical=false` on backfill pool.
Ops Sam: I can push a short-lived mutation and monitor `pod_evictions` and `avg_wait_time` in console. rolling it out in 5.
Maria C: also let's throttle autoscaler scale-ups for 15m so we don't buy new instances while troubleshooting. cost mitigation.
infra-bot: [action] Ops Sam started rollout: relax-gang canary -> us-west2, 10% of nodes (7032104330)
Ops Sam: canary in, watching metrics. so far evictions down 30% and queue depth improved.
Jin H: good. meanwhile I'll open a ticket with networking to look at switch port errors on rack-42. suspect flapping SFP or lane mismatch.
Priya N: after canary stabilizes, plan: 1) cordon affected rack, 2) migrate long-running criticals to pinned dedicated pool, 3) repair hardware.
Alex G: sg. quick note — add a fallback policy in routing so when a gang can't get NVLink-friendly placement we fallback to a multi-node variant (with autoscale guardrails). avoids hard failures.
Maria C: logging action items in infra-runbook and cost channel. tagging @network-team.
infra-bot: [note] thread closed for now — followups in #eng-platform if new errors appear.
